slides.heading: Palindrome Partitioning Min Cuts
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Palindrome Partitioning Min Cuts, a very hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Fewest cuts so every piece is a palindrome.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Fewest cuts so every piece is a palindrome.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Precompute which substrings are palindromes, then fewest cuts for each prefix.
slides.narration: Precompute which substrings are palindromes, then fewest cuts for each prefix.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Trying every partition is exponential. A palindrome table plus a min-cuts DP is quadratic.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Cuts of i is zero if the prefix is a palindrome
3. Otherwise min over j of cuts plus one
slides.narration: Step by step. First, palindrome table by expanding lengths. Second, cuts of i is zero if the prefix is a palindrome. Third, otherwise min over j of cuts plus one.

slides.heading: Worked example

panels.label: min cuts for prefix ending here

slides.caption: cuts[j] = min over palindromes s[i..j] of cuts[i−1] + 1
slides.narration: For each end j, consider every palindrome ending there; the cuts are one more than the best for the prefix before it.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each end j, cuts starts at j; for each start i where s i to j is a palindrome, mark it and update cuts j with zero or cuts i minus one plus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n squared.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: If the whole string is a palindrome, zero cuts.
